evidence: The audited AIOps surface is primarily operational CLI, automation, ledgers and adapters rather than a bounded product UI consumer.
gaps: No revision-bound AI Core UI/UX consumer surface was established as material to this audit.
findings.next_action: Do not invent a UI conformance project for CLI/automation code. Audit a concrete AIOps user interface separately if one becomes an active product surface.

evidence: AIOps distinguishes source facts, canonical finance/receivable projections and operational event ledgers.
Read-only finance adapters fail closed when cash or receivable sources are stale or missing.
Finance adapter projection deliberately omits customer names and vehicle numbers from aggregate AI Core results.
Operational ledger guidance uses append-only correction/cancellation rather than rewriting past events.
gaps: Some operational sources remain local/runtime-dependent and cannot be proven current from GitHub alone.
findings.next_action: Keep source freshness and non-PII projection rules; bind runtime source observations to revision/evidence without copying raw sensitive data into Core.

evidence: AI Core penalty execution uses the existing AIOps engine through a project-module adapter rather than duplicating the engine.
Executor requires an AI Core authority receipt before acquiring drive/firestore/sheet leases.
Process exit alone is insufficient; a new terminal gwataeryo-run-manifest/v1 must exist before success is returned.
COMPLETED_WITH_HOLD and FAILED remain distinct from SUCCEEDED.
Cash and receivable adapters are read-only and preserve stale-source HOLD behavior.
gaps: Insurance adapter remains HOLD and should not be inferred from adjacent operational code.
findings.next_action: Continue capability-by-capability binding; preserve AIOps engine authority and terminal receipt semantics instead of copying operational logic into AI Core.

evidence: Adapters return stable machine blockers such as CASH_SOURCE_GAPS and RECEIVABLE_SOURCE_STALE_* rather than relying on mutable prose.
Penalty execution distinguishes invalid AI Core context, executor identity, unresolved ledger, missing terminal manifest, HOLD and FAILED states.
Audit/event guidance separates append-only events from current projections and uses correction events instead of in-place history rewriting.
gaps: No material public HTTP API boundary was established in this audit, so OpenAPI/HTTP transport conformance was not scored.
findings.next_action: Keep stable blocker/result semantics. Apply the future canonical HTTP profile only to actual API boundaries rather than forcing CLI workflows into HTTP-shaped contracts.

evidence: AIOps distinguishes human completion claims from evidence-verified completion.
Penalty change-charge flow distinguishes review pending from technical transition failure.
Scheduler health distinguishes REVIEW_PENDING, TRANSITION_FAILED, QUOTA_BLOCKED and disabled tasks.
Operational docs define append-only completion history and recurring work reopening as new work rather than reviving old rows.
gaps: The inspected workflow semantics are not bound as an AI Core D workflow/projection consumer at the audited revision.
Actual Windows Task Scheduler Enabled/LastRun/LastTaskResult cannot be proven from GitHub.
findings.next_action: Choose one bounded AIOps lifecycle, preferably penalty review/dispatch or hold-resume scheduling, and add D SHADOW parity while keeping current runtime authority.

evidence: lib/seungin.mjs classifies actions by risk rather than by storage technology alone.
Review/approval is bound to plan SHA, template SHA and target digest; changed subjects invalidate old approval.
Self-review is rejected and independent reviewer substitution is supported.
Approvals have TTL; emergency approval can be command-bound and cannot open protected actions.
Approval records use an append-only hash chain plus a second audit ledger cross-check to detect tampering or full ledger reconstruction.
Tests exercise stale approval, self-review, BLOCK precedence, TTL expiry, command binding, tamper detection and non-overridable protected actions.
gaps: AI Core Security/Audit axis is still RESEARCH_ONLY and cannot issue a normative pass.
test/seungin.test.mjs and test/with-lease-seungin.test.mjs are not included in the current npm test or AI Core Penalty Adapter CI workflow.
Current approval/audit runtime files are local coordination evidence and were not independently inspected.
findings.next_action: Use exact-subject approval, separation-of-duties, TTL, non-overridable action class and dual-ledger tamper evidence as reverse-import inputs for the canonical Security/Audit profile; separately wire their regression tests into required CI before treating the project implementation as continuously enforced.

evidence: Penalty health models task disabled, review pending, transition failure, quota block and success as distinct operational states.
Read-only penalty:health exposes scheduler readiness without mutating scheduler state.
Terminal run manifests make process completion independently checkable.
Finance adapters fail closed on stale source dates rather than presenting stale figures as current.
gaps: AI Core QA/Observability axis remains RESEARCH_ONLY.
Actual scheduler state and heartbeat freshness were not independently observed from the user's Windows host.
Repository-wide verification is fragmented: npm test does not include the approval/lease integration tests.
No canonical OpenTelemetry/health/freshness envelope is bound across the repository.
findings.next_action: Reverse-import health state separation, freshness fail-closed and terminal-manifest proof into the future Core QA/Observability profile; add a checker manifest or unified verification entrypoint so omitted suites cannot silently look green.

evidence: Latest AI Core Penalty Adapter workflow run 35419155299 passed penalty and finance adapter suites at the exact audited revision.
AIOps intentionally has no build artifact and documents build as not applicable.
Project registry revision matches current main.
gaps: main branch protection currently reports protected=false.
ai-core-penalty.yml pull_request paths include lib/ai-core-finance-adapters.mjs and its test, but push paths omit them; a future finance-only main change may skip the dedicated workflow.
test/seungin.test.mjs and test/with-lease-seungin.test.mjs are not required by current CI.
No repository-wide checker manifest declares required/manual/not-applicable suites.
Actual local scheduler enablement remains outside GitHub evidence.
findings.next_action: Fix the finance push-path asymmetry, make approval/lease regression suites required, add an explicit checker manifest/unified verify command, and enable branch protection only after required checks are stable.

limitations: Audit is read-only and covers aiops main at c37a422765e784cdd843f36efb4be5328d7df4bb.
Open PR #6 insurance adapter is not treated as main evidence.
Security/Audit and QA/Observability are research-only AI Core axes and therefore remain advisory.
Actual Windows Task Scheduler state, local coordination ledgers and live Google/Firebase resources were not independently observed.
A passing dedicated workflow does not prove omitted approval/lease suites are enforced.
